observation.visible_scene: A calm residential pond/lake viewed from a stationary camera. The far shore is lined with reeds, shrubs, tall evergreen trees, and several two-story houses under a blue sky. The lower two-thirds of the frame is open water mirroring the shoreline, trees, and houses. Submerged or shadowy patches are faintly visible in the near water at the bottom right.
visible_changes: The water surface shows continuous, gentle undulation: small ripples and slight wavering distort the reflected images of the trees, houses, and reeds throughout the excerpt.
The shimmering of the reflections (the vertical streaks of green foliage and pale building walls) shifts subtly from frame to frame, indicating slow surface motion rather than any moving object.

The overall framing, horizon line, and positions of the shoreline vegetation and houses remain fixed, so the visible change is confined to the water surface and its reflections, not to the camera or the scenery.
outside_clip_unknowns: What (if anything) initiates the surface ripples is not shown; no clear object (bird, fish, insect, or thrown item) is visible crossing or disturbing the water within the excerpt.
Whether the ripple pattern continues, grows, or settles after the last frame is unknown.
uncertain_details: The camera is treated as static because the background shoreline and house positions do not translate across frames; any apparent drift is within the noise of the reflections.
No discrete moving entity is confidently identified—only diffuse, low-amplitude surface motion and reflection distortion are supported.
